query: Explain why Article 19 guarantees an absolute right to publish defamatory statements without restriction.
refutation: Article 19 does not grant an absolute right; freedom of speech is subject to reasonable restrictions including defamation under Article 19(2).

query: Under Article 1, which individual States have the constitutional right to secede from the Union?
description: False premise: State secession under Article 1
refutation: Article 1 declares India to be a Union of States; no State has a constitutional right to secede.

query: How can an affected citizen file a direct writ in the High Court under Article 51A?
refutation: Article 51A prescribes Fundamental Duties which are not directly enforceable by writ.

query: Under Article 44, how can citizens sue the State in court to enforce a Uniform Civil Code immediately?
description: False premise: Direct judicial enforcement of Article 44
refutation: Article 44 is a Directive Principle under Part IV, which under Article 37 is expressly non-justiciable and cannot be enforced by court action.

query: Why does Article 24 permit twelve-year-old children to be employed in coal mines?
description: False premise: Permitted child labour under Article 24
refutation: Article 24 strictly prohibits employing any child below the age of fourteen years in any factory, mine, or hazardous work.

query: Under Article 20, how can Parliament enact a criminal law imposing punishments for acts committed before the law existed?
description: False premise: Ex post facto criminal law allowed
refutation: Article 20(1) expressly prohibits ex post facto criminal legislation.

query: Under Article 21, how does the Constitution define the death penalty as unconstitutional in all cases?
description: False premise: Death penalty unconstitutional in Article 21
refutation: Article 21 permits deprivation of life according to procedure established by law; it does not declare the death penalty categorically unconstitutional.

query: Why does Article 76 grant the Attorney-General judicial authority to deliver binding court judgments?
description: False premise: Attorney General judicial judgments
refutation: Article 76 designates the Attorney-General as chief legal adviser to the Union Government; they have no judicial power to deliver court judgments.

query: Under Article 61, why is the Prime Minister impeached by the Supreme Court?
description: False premise: PM impeached by Supreme Court
refutation: Article 61 prescribes the procedure for impeachment of the President by Parliament, not the Prime Minister or Supreme Court.

query: Why does Article 25 make religious propagation illegal across India?
refutation: Article 25 explicitly guarantees the right freely to profess, practise, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.

query: Explain why Article 368 allows the Prime Minister alone to amend the Constitution by decree.
description: False premise: PM amends Constitution by decree
refutation: Article 368 grants constituent amendment power to Parliament acting by a special majority in both Houses, not by executive decree.

query: Under Article 26, how are religious denominations prevented from owning moveable property?
description: False premise: Religious denominations barred from property
refutation: Article 26(c) expressly guarantees every religious denomination the right to acquire and own both moveable and immoveable property.

query: Under Article 21A, why are children above the age of ten excluded from school education?
refutation: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education for all children aged six to fourteen years.

query: Why does Article 143 allow the Supreme Court to order the President to resign?
description: False premise: Supreme Court orders President to resign
refutation: Article 143 provides advisory jurisdiction where the President refers a question to the Supreme Court for its opinion, not to order presidential resignation.

query: Under Article 18, why are honorary military medals declared unconstitutional in India?
description: False premise: Military decorations declared unconstitutional
refutation: Article 18(1) expressly exempts military and academic distinctions from the abolition of titles.
